/-!
# Conjecture 7.26

by A. V. Kuznetsov

The *ordinal height* of a variety of groups is, by definition, the supremum of the order
types (ordinals) of all chains of its proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion.
It is clear that its cardinality is either finite or countably infinite, or equal to
$\omega_1$. Is every countable ordinal number the ordinal height of some variety?

A variety of groups (in the sense of Birkhoff and H. Neumann) is a class of groups closed
under taking subgroups, homomorphic images and cartesian products; equivalently, it is the
class of all groups satisfying some set of laws. Here a variety is modelled as such a class
of groups in `Type`, and varieties are ordered by inclusion. By Birkhoff's theorem (which holds
inside the universe `Type`, since the laws live in `FreeGroup ℕ` and a variety is determined by
its countable members), these classes correspond bijectively and order-isomorphically to varieties
of groups, so ordinal heights are unchanged; they live in `Ordinal.{1}` because classes of groups
live in `Type 1`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

theorem ordinalHeight_trivialVariety : ordinalHeight trivialVariety = 0 := by

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: the Prop is ∀ α < ω₁, ∃ variety V of groups (Birkhoff/Neumann sense: class closed under subgroups, quotients, direct products, i.e. defined by laws in a countably generated free group) with ordinalHeight V = α, where ordinalHeight V is the supremum over all chains of proper (≠ V) subvarieties of V that are well-ordered by inclusion of their order types; 'countable ordinal' should include finite ordinals (and 0, realised by the trivial variety whose only chain is empty), and the preceding sentences of the statement are a definition and an 'it is clear' remark, not questions.
claims.reviewer_why: c04 models a variety of groups literally as the source/decomposition notes describe (class of groups in `Type` closed under subgroups/injective homs, homomorphic images and arbitrary cartesian products, including the empty product so the trivial group lies in every variety), orders varieties by inclusion, and defines ordinalHeight V as sSup of Ordinal.type over sets C of varieties with every W ∈ C strictly below V and `<` a well-order on C — exactly 'supremum of order types of chains of proper subvarieties well-ordered by inclusion'. It proves the set of order types is nonempty and bounded (so sSup is the genuine LUB, no junk value) and the boundary case ordinalHeight trivialVariety = 0. Statement: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ α : Ordinal.{1}, α.card ≤ ℵ₀ → ∃ V, ordinalHeight V = α, with countable including 0 and finite ordinals. Universes are pinned (Ordinal.{1}). I only added a module-docstring note explaining why restricting to universe `Type` does not change the lattice of varieties (Birkhoff's theorem goes through inside `Type`; I re-derived the argument). c05/c06 are equivalent but have less API; c01 is equivalent (IsVariety predicate on classes) but slightly less idiomatic. c08 (fully invariant subgroups of FreeGroup ℕ, order-dual) is also faithful and universe-clean but has no API tests and requires the reader to know the Neumann correspondence. c02/c03 are faithful in content but accidentally universe-polymorphic (`theorem.{u}`, `ordinalHeight.{u}`). c07 is unfaithful: `ℵ₀` was never opened and became an auto-bound implicit, so the theorem quantifies over an arbitrary cardinal `{ℵ₀ : Cardinal}`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.26

by A. V. Kuznetsov

The *ordinal height* of a variety of groups is, by definition, the supremum of the order
types (ordinals) of all chains of its proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion.
It is clear that its cardinality is either finite or countably infinite, or equal to
$\omega_1$. Is every countable ordinal number the ordinal height of some variety?

A variety of groups (in the sense of Birkhoff and H. Neumann) is a class of groups closed
under taking subgroups, homomorphic images and cartesian products; equivalently, it is the
class of all groups satisfying some set of laws. Here a variety is modelled as such a class
of groups in `Type`, and varieties are ordered by inclusion. By Birkhoff's theorem (which holds
inside the universe `Type`, since the laws live in `FreeGroup ℕ` and a variety is determined by
its countable members), these classes correspond bijectively and order-isomorphically to varieties
of groups, so ordinal heights are unchanged; they live in `Ordinal.{1}` because classes of groups
live in `Type 1`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Cardinal

namespace Kourovka.«7.26»

/-- A variety of groups: a class of groups (here, of groups in `Type`) that is closed under
taking subgroups, homomorphic images and cartesian products. -/
@[ext]
structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The class of groups belonging to the variety. -/
  Mem : (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop
  /-- A variety is closed under taking subgroups (up to isomorphism). -/
  mem_of_injective {G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H] (f : H →* G) :
    Function.Injective f → Mem G → Mem H
  /-- A variety is closed under taking homomorphic images. -/
  mem_of_surjective {G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H) :
    Function.Surjective f → Mem G → Mem H
  /-- A variety is closed under taking cartesian products. -/
  mem_pi {ι : Type} {G : ι → Type} [∀ i, Group (G i)] :
    (∀ i, Mem (G i)) → Mem (∀ i, G i)

/-- Varieties are ordered by inclusion: `V ≤ W` iff every group in `V` lies in `W`. -/
instance : PartialOrder GroupVariety where
  le V W := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Mem G → W.Mem G
  le_refl _ _ _ := id
  le_trans _ _ _ h₁ h₂ G _ hG := h₂ G (h₁ G hG)
  le_antisymm V W h₁ h₂ :=
    GroupVariety.ext (funext fun G => funext fun _ => propext ⟨h₁ G, h₂ G⟩)

/-- The set of order types of the chains of proper subvarieties of `V` that are well-ordered
by inclusion. -/
def chainOrderTypes (V : GroupVariety) : Set Ordinal.{1} :=
  {o | ∃ (C : Set GroupVariety) (_ : IsWellOrder C (· < ·)),
    (∀ W ∈ C, W < V) ∧ Ordinal.type (α := C) (· < ·) = o}

/-- The ordinal height of a variety `V`: the supremum of the order types of all chains of
proper subvarieties of `V` that are well-ordered by inclusion. -/
noncomputable def ordinalHeight (V : GroupVariety) : Ordinal.{1} :=
  sSup (chainOrderTypes V)

/-- The empty chain contributes the order type `0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem zero_mem_chainOrderTypes (V : GroupVariety) : 0 ∈ chainOrderTypes V :=
  ⟨∅, inferInstance, fun _ h => h.elim, Ordinal.type_eq_zero_of_empty _⟩

/-- The order types of well-ordered chains of subvarieties are bounded, so `ordinalHeight` is a
genuine supremum. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem bddAbove_chainOrderTypes (V : GroupVariety) : BddAbove (chainOrderTypes V) := by
  refine ⟨(Order.succ #GroupVariety).ord, ?_⟩
  rintro o ⟨C, _, -, rfl⟩
  exact (lt_ord.2 (Order.lt_succ_iff.2 ((Ordinal.card_type _).le.trans (mk_set_le C)))).le

/-- `ordinalHeight V` is the least upper bound of the order types of the well-ordered chains of
proper subvarieties of `V`. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem isLUB_ordinalHeight (V : GroupVariety) : IsLUB (chainOrderTypes V) (ordinalHeight V) :=
  isLUB_csSup ⟨0, zero_mem_chainOrderTypes V⟩ (bddAbove_chainOrderTypes V)

/-- The trivial variety, consisting of the trivial groups. -/
def trivialVariety : GroupVariety where
  Mem G _ := Subsingleton G
  mem_of_injective _ hf _ := hf.subsingleton
  mem_of_surjective _ hf _ := hf.subsingleton
  mem_pi h := by
    haveI := h
    infer_instance

/-- Every variety contains the trivial groups, so the trivial variety is the smallest variety. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem trivialVariety_le (V : GroupVariety) : trivialVariety ≤ V := by
  intro G _ hG
  haveI : Subsingleton G := hG
  exact V.mem_of_surjective (1 : (∀ _ : Empty, Unit) →* G)
    (fun g => ⟨1, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩) (V.mem_pi fun i => i.elim)

/-- The trivial variety has no proper subvarieties, so its ordinal height is `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem ordinalHeight_trivialVariety : ordinalHeight trivialVariety = 0 := by
  have h : chainOrderTypes trivialVariety = {0} := by
    refine Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.2 ⟨zero_mem_chainOrderTypes _, ?_⟩
    rintro o ⟨C, _, hC, rfl⟩
    haveI : IsEmpty C := ⟨fun W => ((hC W W.2).trans_le (trivialVariety_le W)).false⟩
    exact Ordinal.type_eq_zero_of_empty _
  rw [ordinalHeight, h, csSup_singleton]

/--
The *ordinal height* of a variety of groups is the supremum of the order types (ordinals) of all
chains of its proper subvarieties that are well-ordered by inclusion. Is every countable ordinal
number the ordinal height of some variety?

Here a countable ordinal is an ordinal $\alpha$ with $|\alpha| \le \aleph_0$; in particular the
finite ordinals are included.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.26» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ α : Ordinal.{1}, α.card ≤ ℵ₀ → ∃ V : GroupVariety, ordinalHeight V = α := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.26»

items: Varieties are modelled as classes of groups living in `Type` (universe 0), closed under cartesian products indexed by types in `Type`, following the Kourovka files' convention of quantifying over `Type`. Birkhoff's theorem goes through inside a fixed universe, so the lattice of such varieties is isomorphic to the lattice of all varieties (equivalently, anti-isomorphic to fully invariant subgroups of the free group of countably infinite rank); hence ordinal heights are unchanged.
Closure under subgroups and homomorphic images is phrased via injective and surjective `MonoidHom`s, which builds in closure under isomorphism (standard for HSP classes).

Closure under cartesian products includes the empty product, so every variety contains the trivial groups and the class of trivial groups is the least variety (Neumann's convention; the empty class is not a variety). Consequently the trivial variety has ordinal height 0, as the decomposition notes expect (proved as a `test` lemma).

'Chain of proper subvarieties well-ordered by inclusion' is `C : Set GroupVariety` with `∀ W ∈ C, W < V` and `IsWellOrder C (· < ·)` (trichotomy gives the chain condition, well-foundedness gives well-ordering); its order type is `Ordinal.type (α := C) (· < ·)`. The empty chain is allowed (order type 0).

The supremum is `sSup` on `Ordinal.{1}` (ordinals live in universe 1 because `GroupVariety : Type 1`); API lemmas show the set of order types is nonempty and bounded above, so `sSup` is the true least upper bound and no junk value is involved.
'Countable ordinal' is rendered as `α.card ≤ ℵ₀` (as in ErdosProblems/592), which includes 0 and all finite ordinals; this is equivalent to `α < ω₁`.
The sentence 'It is clear that its cardinality is either finite or countably infinite, or equal to ω₁' is a remark, not a question, and is not formalized (consistent with the decomposition table).

statement_tex:
The {\it ordinal height\/} of a variety of groups is, by
definition, the supremum of order types (ordinals) of all
well-ordered by inclusion chains of its proper subvarieties. It is
clear that its cardinality is either finite or countably infinite,
or equal to $\omega _1$. Is every countable ordinal number the
ordinal height of some variety?
title: Conjecture 7.26
